Best Local AI Models for NVIDIA Tesla P100 (16GB)

The Tesla P100 PCIe 16GB is a Pascal data-center card with 16GB of HBM2 at 732 GB/s. It holds dense models up to 14B at Q4: an 8B model runs at est. 42 tok/s, typical error 5% and a 14B model at est. 25 tok/s, typical error 15%. Ollama still supports it, but compute capability 6.0 needs NVIDIA driver 570 or newer.

Last updated: November 9, 2026 · Editor: ModelFit Team

Compare with another device
Quick answer

The best local LLM for the Tesla P100 is Mellum2.1 12B-A2.5B Thinking (est. 84 tok/s, typical error 15%) on its 16GB VRAM. It uses ~8.1GB of VRAM; the Tesla P100 handles dense models up to ~14B at Q4. A 14B model at Q4 runs at est. 25 tok/s, typical error 15%. (ModelFit, 2026)

Sizing rule: a Q4 model needs about 0.6 GB of VRAM per billion parameters for its weights, and ModelFit budgets 90% of this card's 16GB (14.4GB) for weights, context, and KV-cache. Real files often load more than that rule, so the per-size table below checks actual builds: a size fits only when the lightest Q4 build of that size in our catalog loads within 14.4GB. MoE rows, and sizes with no such build, use a typical Q4 file size. Other strong fits: Gemma 4 12B (12B, ~8GB) and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B (4B, ~7.9GB). On this card Mellum2.1 12B-A2.5B Thinking runs at est. 84 tok/s, typical error 15%. What it will not run: a 32B model does not fit in VRAM alone, so it spills to system RAM over PCIe and slows sharply.

ModelFit estimates, not measured benchmarks: decode speed of a generic Q4_K_M model of each size at 4K context on the Tesla P100's 732 GB/s bandwidth. MoE rows scale by active parameters (decode reads only the active experts), so a 35B MoE runs far faster than a dense 32B. "CPU offload" sizes exceed the 16GB VRAM; dense models slow to a crawl there, MoE models degrade less because hot experts stay GPU-resident. Offload rows are rough estimates: no measured run covers offload, so they carry no typical error. What typical error means.

Fig. 2

Context costs VRAM too.

Mellum2.1 12B-A2.5B Thinking loads ~8.1 GB of weights; at 16k context the KV cache adds ~0.2 GB (still fits the ~14 GB usable VRAM), and at 64k it adds ~0.9 GB (still fits).

Weights 8.1 GBKV cache · 16k context 0.2 GBHeadroom 6.1 GBRuntime reserve 1.6 GB

The model leaves about 6.1 GB of the usable VRAM budget free after weights and 16k context.

KV-cache figures assume an fp16 cache, the llama.cpp/Ollama default. Standard GQA models use a size-class estimate (8 KV heads x 128 head dim class); hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3.5/3.6, Qwen3-Next) use the exact per-token cost from their published config, since only their sparse full-attention layers cache KV. A q8_0 KV cache roughly halves either figure. Estimates, not measurements.

Tesla P100 VRAM for AI: what actually fits?

ModelFit budgets about 14.4GB of the 16GB for weights and context, so 14B models at Q4 (~11GB) load with room for context. Its 732 GB/s is more raw bandwidth than the RTX 5060 Ti (448 GB/s), but Pascal and HBM cards decode below their raw bandwidth in the measured runs the speed model is fitted on, so the estimate is est. 42 tok/s, typical error 5% against est. 68 tok/s on 8B. Prompt reading is the weak side: its FP16 rate is 18.7 TFLOPS with no tensor cores, a fraction of an RTX card, which the first-token times below reflect.

Tesla P100 FAQ: common questions

How much VRAM does the Tesla P100 have?

The Tesla P100 PCIe has 16GB of HBM2 at 732 GB/s (NVIDIA datasheet). ModelFit budgets about 14.4GB of it for weights and context, enough for dense models up to 14B at Q4 quantization.

Does Ollama support the Tesla P100?

Yes. Ollama lists the Tesla P100 under compute capability 6.0 in its NVIDIA support table. Cards of compute capability 5.0 to 6.2 need NVIDIA driver version 570 or newer.

What size LLM can I run on a Tesla P100 16GB?

Dense models up to 14B at Q4, such as Qwen3 14B (~11GB) at est. 25 tok/s, typical error 15%. 8B models run at est. 42 tok/s, typical error 5% with room for a long context. 27B and 32B dense models spill into system RAM.

Tesla P100 vs RTX 5060 Ti 16GB for local AI?

Both hold 16GB. The 5060 Ti is estimated at est. 68 tok/s, typical error 5% on 8B against est. 42 tok/s for the P100, and its tensor cores read prompts much faster. The P100 is a passively cooled 250 W server card (NVIDIA datasheet) that needs case airflow built for it; the 5060 Ti is a desktop card with its own fans.

How fast is a 27B-class model on the Tesla P100?

The Tesla P100's 16GB of VRAM cannot fit a 32B model comfortably. The largest size class it fits is 20B MoE (3.6B active), at est. 57 tok/s, typical error 15%. The largest individual model in the catalog that fits is LFM2 24B-A2B Instruct (24B).
